Title: Power restored in parts of Sandakan, Lahad Datu and Kunak
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Electricity supply has been restored to several areas in Sandakan, Lahad Datu and Kunak tonight following an outage caused by a disruption to the transmission line from the west coast.
Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd, in a statement, said the main areas in Sandakan where supply had been restored included Sandakan Sports Complex, Sandakan Prison, Utama Park Villa Phases 1 and 2, Garden Villa, Utama Sri Condo Blocks A and B, Utama Court, Jalan Sibuga, Taman Mawar and Taman Anggerik.
In Lahad Datu, the main areas where supply had been restored included Lahad Datu Hospital, the Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esccom) office, Lahad Datu District Office, Lahad Datu District Police Headquarters, Lahad Datu Health Clinic, Lahad Datu District Council, Fish Market, People's Market, Taman Fajar and Jalan Tengah Nipah.
In Kunak, the main areas where supply had been restored included Kunak town, Kampung Kunak Kecil, the District Office, Sime Darby Police Station, the port and surrounding areas.
"Sabah Electricity apologises for any inconvenience caused during the disruption and greatly appreciates the patience and cooperation of its customers," it said.
Meanwhile, Sabah Electricity said a viral message circulating, particularly on social media, claiming that electricity supply along Sabah's east coast would be disrupted for two weeks was fake.
The company advised the public not to be misled by viral messages, to verify information before sharing it and to obtain the latest updates only through its official platforms.
Customers seeking clarification may call 15444 or 088-515000 for verification, while enquiries or complaints can also be submitted via WhatsApp at 019-8525427.

Title: Six days to restore Sabah east coast grid, riverbank erosion caused tower collapse
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd (Sabah Electricity) is targeting six days to fully restore the 275kV transmission grid supplying Sabah's east coast after a transmission tower collapsed in Ranau early today.
Its chairman, Datuk Saadiah Aziz, said the grid was expected to be fully restored by Dec 2, following the reconnection of two affected transmission lines.
She said the six-day period would allow Sabah Electricity and its contractors to transport equipment to the site, install temporary towers and reconnect the lines at a location deemed safe near the collapsed tower.
In the meantime, electricity supply to the east coast would be generated using existing power plants in Sandakan and Tawau, supplemented by mobile generators deployed to affected areas.
"We are targeting six days to reconnect the grid supplying Sabah's east coast, and the work may be completed earlier.
"However, what is important is that we also prioritise the safety of those carrying out the work on the ground.
"We hope everything goes smoothly so that electricity supply to consumers on the east coast can return to normal," she said in a press conference at Sabah Electricity's headquarters.
Also present was its chief executive officer, Datuk Mohd Yaakob Jaafar.
Saadiah said Sabah Electricity activated its crisis management system after identifying the cause of the power disruption on the east coast and immediately drew up measures to temporarily restore supply in seven affected districts.
The tower collapse disrupted electricity supply in Sandakan, Beluran, Kinabatangan, Lahad Datu, Kunak, Semporna and Tawau, affecting 153,599 registered consumers.
"We managed the situation well, beginning with the reopening of the main Ranau-Telupid road, which was blocked by an electricity cable near SK Matupang in Ranau this morning.
"This was followed by efforts to restore electricity supply in stages to the affected districts using existing and mobile generators," she said.
She said Sabah Electricity had since managed to integrate the east coast grid, connecting all districts in the region to improve supply capacity and limit scheduled power rationing to between one and two hours.
Meanwhile, Yaakob said erosion along the banks of Sungai Liwagu in Ranau, caused by strong currents following continuous rain, was identified as the main reason transmission tower T313 collapsed.
He said the riverbank erosion had been detected in January, prompting reinforcement works in March using sandbags and large rocks.
"However, strong currents in Sungai Liwagu following continuous rain in Ranau over the past few days washed away the newly reinforced riverbank, eventually causing the tower to collapse," he said.
The incident resulted in the east coast losing 295MW of electricity supplied from Sabah's west coast.
Yaakob said grid restoration would begin with the first transmission line, which was expected to be reconnected on Dec 1, followed by the second line on Dec 2, allowing Sabah's grid system to be fully restored.

Title: Govt wants listed companies to adopt RM3,400 living wage benchmark
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has called on public-listed companies (PLCs) to adopt the RM3,400 living wage benchmark across their organisations.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said fair and adequate wages would enable employees to meet their basic needs and maintain a decent standard of living.
He said this could also contribute to greater workforce stability, better talent retention and higher productivity.
"This is an important dimension of responsible business conduct, recognising that long-term corporate value creation must also take into account the well-being and economic security of the people who contribute to it.
"Paying a living wage is verifiable proof to investors, regulators and consumers that the social pillar of your sustainability report is backed by real conviction," he said at the 2026 National Annual Corporate Report Awards (NACRA) presentation dinner.
Amir Hamzah said the government remained committed to strengthening the institutional and policy foundations for sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
"Good governance, accountability and transparency are integral to this agenda, particularly as Malaysia seeks to move towards higher-value economic activities and strengthen its position in the global economy," said Amir Hamzah.
He said stronger governance and reporting practices could help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) improve management discipline, assess business performance, access financing and engage more effectively with investors and business partners.
These capabilities are increasingly important as SMEs seek to expand their operations and participate in larger domestic and international value chains.
Amir Hamzah also said companies must invest in developing their workforce capabilities, particularly in data analytics, sustainability and environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, climate finance and digital finance.
"These competencies are important not only for meeting new reporting requirements, but also for understanding business risks, evaluating investment decisions and supporting long-term strategy," he added.
Meanwhile, 2026 NACRA organising committee chairman Ong Chee Wai said high-quality corporate reporting was essential to building stakeholder trust, reinforcing investor confidence and supporting sustainable business growth among Malaysian companies.
"It also provides a competitive edge, helping organisations to attract investment and compete more effectively in an increasingly interconnected global economy.
"Through NACRA, we seek to recognise organisations that demonstrate these qualities and encourage continuous improvement across the corporate sector," he said
Ong said the awards provided an opportunity for organisations to benchmark their practices against leading examples and raise the overall standard of corporate reporting in Malaysia.
Themed "Towards Accountability and Excellence", NACRA 2026 is jointly organised by Bursa Malaysia Bhd, the Malaysian Institute of Accountants and the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

Title: TNB delivers sustained financial & operational resilience, absorbs fuel costs to shield consumers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) continues to deliver sustained financial and operational resilience for the nine months ended Sept 30 2026, strengthening the group's ability to cushion consumers from rising global fuel costs.
Its customer protection efforts are expected to benefit more than eight million domestic electricity users, or up to 90 per cent of the segment, reflecting TNB's efforts to balance consumer interests, financial sustainability and long-term investment needs to meet the country's energy demand.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, TNB recorded revenue of RM53.9 billion, compared with RM50.1 billion in the corresponding period last year.
The group's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) stood at RM16.1 billion.
In a statement accompanying its financial results, TNB said the group's resilient performance was supported by higher electricity sales, disciplined financial management and continued efforts to improve operational efficiency across its businesses.
Putting Customers First Amid Global Fuel Pressures
TNB has reinforced its commitment to protecting electricity customers from rising global fuel costs through close cooperation with the government.
Against the backdrop of global fuel market uncertainties, including challenges arising from developments in West Asia, TNB remains focused on managing costs responsibly, supporting customers and sustaining the financial strength needed to meet Malaysia's growing energy requirements.
As global fuel cost pressures continue to affect energy markets, TNB and the government have undertaken coordinated measures to cushion customers from the impact of rising costs, while ensuring the continued reliability and sustainability of electricity supply.
While fuel cost fluctuations are reflected through the government-approved Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) mechanism, TNB has also taken proactive measures to support customer protection.
TNB is estimated to absorb up to RM150 million in AFA and retail charges following the expansion of the domestic customer protection threshold from 600 kWh to 800 kWh per month between September and December 2026.
This benefitted more than eight million, or up to 90 per cent of domestic customers.
These measures serve as an investment to forge long-term trust and regulatory stability, building the foundation for TNB's sustainable returns.
This complements the government's RM435 million injections from the Electricity Industry Fund (KWIE) to moderate AFA surcharges for May to August 2026.
Customers had also received RM3.1 billion in AFA rebates between July 2025 and April 2026, reflecting the mechanism's response to movements in global fuel costs.
Together, these measures reflect the close cooperation between TNB and the government in managing global fuel cost pressures while prioritising the interests and wellbeing of electricity customers.
Beyond cost mitigation, TNB continued empowering customers to manage their electricity consumption.
The myTNB app enables customers to monitor their electricity usage, while its Energy Budget feature helps them plan and manage monthly consumption.
The Time-of-Use (ToU) mechanism further provides eligible customers to manage costs by shifting usage to off-peak periods.
TNB President/Chief Executive Officer Datuk Seri Ir. Ts. Shamsul Ahmad said the group remains committed to supporting customers while sustaining the operational and financial resilience required to deliver reliable electricity and prepare Malaysia's energy system for future growth.
"Our responsibility goes beyond keeping the lights on. It is about ensuring that households have reliable electricity for everyday life, businesses have the energy they need to grow, and Malaysia has a resilient electricity system capable of supporting its economic ambitions," he said.
Keeping Malaysia Powered
TNB continues to maintain dependable electricity amid increasing demand driven by industrial expansion under the Malaysia's New Industrial Master Plan 2030, the growing digital economy and rising investments in data centres.
Electricity demand grew by 8.3 per cent year-on-year to 108.2 TWh, supported by increased consumption from the commercial and domestic sectors, alongside expanding economic activities and growing energy requirements from data centres, digital infrastructure and retail businesses.
Meanwhile, the System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) improved to 34.90 minutes from 34.99 minutes during the corresponding period last year.
This reflects TNB's continued focus on operational performance and supply reliability, supported by preventive maintenance, network automation and operational readiness.
Advancing Malaysia's Energy Transition Ambitions
In support of Malaysia's National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), TNB continues investing in critical energy infrastructure to accelerate renewable energy integration, enhance grid flexibility and ensure a reliable electricity supply as the nation transitions towards a low-carbon economy.
In the first nine months of 2026, the group invested RM9.1 billion in reliability-related projects, supporting the development of a modern, resilient electricity system capable of accommodating growing demand and a more diversified energy mix.
Key initiatives include:
* 500 kV National Grid Backbone: Development of a 500-kilometre transmission backbone, targeted for completion by 2030, to strengthen grid connectivity and facilitate future energy integration.
* Battery Energy Storage System (BESS): Commissioning of the 100-megawatt/400-megawatt-hour BESS in Santong, Terengganu, which was recognised as Malaysia's first grid-connected, grid-forming BESS.
* Regasification Terminal 3 (RGT-3): Collaboration with Petronas Gas Bhd to develop the facility in Lumut, Perak, enhancing long-term liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply resilience to support reliable electricity generation.
TNB also advanced regional energy connectivity through the Asean Power Grid (APG), including recent progress on the Vietnam–Malaysia–Singapore (VMS) cross-border electricity initiative, which aims to facilitate renewable energy exports from Vietnam through Malaysia to Singapore.
TNB remains committed in working closely with the government to ensure Malaysia's energy transition is delivered in an orderly, affordable and secure manner.
A stable and predictable regulatory environment will be critical to sustaining the investments needed for grid modernisation and renewable energy integration.
Creating Values For Communities And The Nation
Beyond electricity supply, TNB continued contributing to Malaysia's sustainable development through environmental conservation, education and community empowerment.
Throughout the period, the group chanelled RM186 million towards community development and corporate social responsibility initiatives, including:
* Education (RM133.2 million): Support through UNITEN and Yayasan Tenaga Nasional, benefitting 218,000 students.
* Economic and Social (RM23.3 million): School assistance, community electrification, disaster relief and Projek Mesra rakyat, benefitting 225,000 individuals.
* Sports Development (RM12.4 million): Hockey development and other sports initiatives, benefitting 54,000 athletes and sports enthusiasts.
* Environmental Protection (RM3.0 million):MyBrighter Green and other conservation initiatives.
* Nation Building (RM14.2 million): Initiative supporting energy transition awareness, national unity and technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
Additionally, RM10.6 million in zakat wakalah was channelled to over 60,000 asnaf beneficiaries.
Sustaining Performance To Deliver Long-Term Value
TNB's resilient performance was supported by higher electricity sales, disciplined financial management and continued efforts to optimise operational efficiency across its businesses.
TNB's achievements also gained recognition locally and internationally, including Brand of the Year 2026-2027 at the World Branding Awards, Power Utility of the Year at EnlitAsia, and Best Public Utility App for myTNB by PC.comReaders' Choice Awards 2026, reflecting its operational excellence, brand strength and customer-centric digital innovation.
Staying Focused On Malaysia's Energy Future
Looking ahead, TNB expects electricity demand to be influenced by commercial growth, digitalisation and expanding energy requirements, while remaining mindful of global fuel market uncertainties.
TNB remains committed towards prioritising investments aligned with the NETR, particularly grid modernisation, renewable energy integration and system readiness, to support Malaysia's economic growth and transition towards a sustainable energy future.
"TNB will continue balancing operational reliability, financial discipline and long-term investments to meet Malaysia's evolving energy needs. Our focus remains on delivering secure electricity today while building a stronger, more sustainable energy system for tomorrow," Shamsul said.

Title: Nine Kelantan districts at risk of flooding until Nov 30
Article:
KOTA BARU: Nine districts in Kelantan are at risk of flooding until Nov 30 following a continuous rain warning issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today.
According to the Kelantan Early Flood Forecast, updated at 8pm, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) identified Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah, Tumpat, Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Machang and Kuala Krai as areas at risk.
DID said potential flood-affected areas include known flood hotspots, low-lying areas and risk zones along several major river basins in the state.
The Golok River basin covers Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah and Tumpat, while the Kelantan River basin involves Kota Bharu, Machang and Kuala Krai.
In Pasir Puteh and Bachok, the risk areas cover the Semerak River basin, as well as the Kelantan River in Pasir Puteh and the Kemasin and Gali rivers in Bachok.
DID said continuous monitoring would be carried out, with flood warnings issued if significant rainfall persisted in the river basins.
It added that flooding could occur earlier or later than forecast.
Disaster management agencies and residents, particularly those in areas at risk, were advised to remain vigilant and follow instructions from the authorities.
The public can obtain the latest flood information and warnings via publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my and the PublicInfoBanjir Facebook page.

Title: 'It breaks my heart': Father mourns 2 sons killed in crash
Article:
KOTA BARU: "It was heartbreaking to see my two children lying there covered in blood," said Saiful Nizam Abdul Sani, 42, whose two sons were
killed
in a motorcycle crash in Kampung Bechah Tendong, Pasir Mas, today.
His eldest son, Muhammad Saiful Haikal, 18, who was riding the motorcycle, was injured and is receiving treatment at Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZ II).
Saiful Nizam said the accident occurred as Saiful Haikal was taking his two younger brothers home after picking them up from kindergarten and school.
He said the eldest had first fetched Muhammad Saiful Hayyan from kindergarten before returning home to wait until it was time to pick up Muhammad Saiful Haider from Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Othman Talib 1.
"When he was about to leave to collect Muhammad Saiful Haider, his younger brother also asked to go along.
"They were involved in the accident while travelling home to Kampung Bechah Tendong, about 1km from the scene," he said when met at the HRPZ II Forensic Department today.
Saiful Nizam said he received a call from his wife, Nur Zuhanis Mohd Noor, 42, about 2pm, informing him of the accident after a nearby food stall operator contacted her.
"I rushed to the scene and found two of my children lying there covered in blood. It was a heartbreaking sight.
"Saiful Haider died at the scene, while Saiful Hayyan died on the way to HRPZ II.
"Saiful Haikal is now receiving treatment at the hospital's emergency department," he said.
He also recalled that Saiful Hayyan's kindergarten teacher had noticed a change in the boy's behaviour that day, saying he had been unusually quiet.
"His teacher told me that Saiful Hayyan was usually cheerful, active and friendly, but he seemed different today," he said.
The remains of the two brothers will be buried at the Kampung Gaung Muslim cemetery in Tendong, Pasir Mas, after the post-mortem.

Title: Genting falls into the red in Q3 with RM161.4mil net loss
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Bhd posted a net loss of RM161.4 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), compared with a net profit of RM30.3 million a year earlier.
Genting's quarterly revenue rose 7.3 per cent to RM8.02 billion from RM7.48 billion.
For the nine months of FY26, the group recorded a net loss of RM87.4 million, against a net profit of RM278.4 million in the corresponding period last year.
Its revenue for the nine-month period increased eight per cent to RM22.43 billion from RM20.77 billion.
Genting said the lower quarterly profit was mainly due to lower earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda), higher finance costs, lower interest income and a smaller share of profits from joint ventures and associates.
The group's leisure and hospitality and plantation divisions were the main contributors to revenue growth during the quarter.
However, its Resorts World Sentosa and Resorts World Genting operations recorded lower revenue and Ebitda.
Genting said it remained cautious about its near-term prospects amid geopolitical tensions, macroeconomic uncertainty and cost pressures, and would continue to focus on operational efficiency and cost discipline.

Title: Teen believed to have lost control before crash killed 2 brothers
Article:
PASIR MAS: Police believe an 18-year-old motorcyclist lost control of his motorcycle before it crashed into a lamp post and a pothole, killing his two younger brothers in Tendong here today.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan said the three siblings were travelling home on a Yamaha LC110 when the motorcycle skidded along the Tendong-Bunut Susu road in Kampung Bechah about 2pm.
"The impact threw all three off the motorcycle.
"The 10-year-old boy died at the scene from severe head injuries, while his six-year-old brother died while receiving treatment at the emergency department of Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZ II) in Kota Baru," he said.
Mazlan said the eldest brother, who was riding the motorcycle, sustained head injuries and remained under treatment at the same hospital.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He reminded parents to pay closer attention to their children's road safety and ensure they wear helmets when riding motorcycles.
He also cautioned against carrying more than two people on a motorcycle, saying the practice was illegal and posed a safety risk.
"Police will continue enforcement operations to ensure road users comply with traffic regulations, while educating the public on the importance of road safety," he said.

two siblings were killed
while their 18-year-old brother was injured when the motorcycle they were riding skidded and overturned in Tendong.

Title: Discipline teacher cleared of physical assault, jailed over sexual remarks
Article:
TAWAU: A secondary school discipline teacher was acquitted by the Sessions Court today of physically sexually assaulting a 17-year-old student four years ago.
However, he was sentenced to two years in prison and two strokes of the rotan for non-physical sexual assault involving another student.
Judge Ahmad Faizadh Yahaya imposed a one-year jail term for the offence, with an additional one-year jail term and two strokes of the cane under Section 16 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The court took into account that the 37-year-old accused was a teacher who held a position of trust over the victim.
On the first charge, the accused was alleged to have physically sexually assaulted a 17-year-old student in the library of a secondary school here around noon on Feb 15, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.
In his judgment, Faizadh said there was reasonable doubt over whether the accused had access to the library, where the alleged offence took place.
He said the accused's denial of having access to the room was supported by documents showing that he had been assigned to mark Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination papers at the time.
The court therefore ruled that the defence had succeeded in raising reasonable doubt over the first charge, before acquitting and discharging him at the close of the defence case.
On the second charge, the accused was alleged to have committed non-physical sexual assault by making sexually explicit remarks and holding and pulling the hand of another 17-year-old student for sexual purposes at the same location about 9.20am on April 19, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 15(a) of Act 792, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.
Faizadh said it was undisputed that the accused held a position of trust over the victim and was the only teacher who was not attached to the library but had permission to use it and hold its keys at the time.
He said the court found that the victim's testimony on the sexually explicit remarks and the act of pulling her hand remained consistent and was not shaken during cross-examination by the defence.
The judge also noted that the accused had admitted to touching the victim's hand when handing over a mobile phone.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Opposition leader questions Achi Jaya's Boustead Plantations bid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin says it is against the proposed takeover of Boustead Plantations Bhd by Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd, questioning the prospect of a strategic plantation asset coming under foreign ownership.
Hamzah said the opposition will not support the proposed sale, claiming that Boustead Plantations was set to be acquired by a company owned by foreigners.
He said the development was concerning, particularly after an earlier attempt to sell part of the plantation group's stake to a Malaysian company had faced opposition from the then opposition bloc.
"Today, there is something else happening. Boustead already has an agreement, and we have heard from sources within the country that Boustead Plantations will be sold to a company owned by 'foreigners'.
"We, the opposition, do not agree with this at all," he said.
Hamzah added that the opposition will issue a formal statement to register its objection to the proposed transaction.
His remarks come after reports that the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) had selected Achi Jaya Plantations to acquire Boustead Plantations in a deal estimated at RM4.3 billion.
Achi Jaya reportedly emerged ahead of competing bidders SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd, both of which have substantially larger plantation operations.
The reported selection has raised questions over the evaluation criteria used by LTAT, particularly given the scale of the bidders and their respective operational track records.
Pasir Mas MP Ahmad Fadhli Shaari had also called on LTAT to explain why Achi Jaya was preferred over the two larger plantation groups.
Achi Jaya is a privately held company incorporated in 2001, with interests in oil palm cultivation and milling, as well as hotel management and operations.
According to its November 2025 Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil certification audit, the company's operations within the scope of certification comprised 11,702 hectares of oil palm planted area across three estates in Johor.
In comparison, Boustead Plantations has a land bank of 97,500 hectares, including about 72,200 hectares of planted oil palm areas.
The acquisition could therefore significantly expand Achi Jaya's plantation footprint, although the actual scale of the combined operations would depend on the assets and equity interests covered by the transaction.
A check on Achi Jaya's shareholding structure reportedly found links to Tan Sri Onn Mahmud, the younger brother of former Sarawak chief minister and governor Tun Abdul Taib Mahmud.
Grand Shine Trading Ltd and Herolite Investment Ltd each hold 36.89 per cent stakes in Achi Jaya, while Onn's company, Achi Jaya Holdings, holds 14.3 per cent.
Onn also has a direct 11.91 per cent interest in the company.
The proposed takeover comes three years after an earlier attempt to sell a 33 per cent stake in Boustead Plantations to Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) for RM1.15 billion was terminated in October 2023.
The proposed transaction had valued Boustead Plantations at RM3.47 billion, but faced political resistance over concerns that LTAT would relinquish control of a strategic plantation asset to a non-Bumiputera company.
The latest reported RM4.3 billion price tag is about RM830 million, or 23.9 per cent, higher than the valuation under the previous KLK proposal, although a direct comparison would depend on the final transaction structure and the equity interest involved.

Title: Teen gets warning after admitting to cyberbullying
Article:
TAWAU: An 18-year-old student who pleaded guilty to uploading a 13-year-old girl's photograph on social media with threatening captions was discharged with a warning by the magistrate's court today.
Magistrate Don Stiwin Malanjum made the ruling under Section 91(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 (Amendment 2016) after taking into account recommendations from the Social Welfare Department.
The court also considered that the eldest of five siblings regretted his actions, had promised not to reoffend and wanted to focus on his studies.
The court also ordered the return of his RM500 bail.
According to the charge, the accused, who was 17 at the time of the offence, had uploaded the photograph of the victim, then 13, at a restaurant at noon on April 17.
He was charged under Section 507E of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Based on the facts of the case, the victim's mother received a WhatsApp message from a friend containing a screenshot of her daughter's photograph on Instagram, accompanied by several captions making allegations of bullying and threats.
Investigations found that the accused had uploaded the photograph after reading a WhatsApp group conversation claiming that a friend's cousin had been bullied by the victim and another individual.
The accused admitted that he had acted on impulse before obtaining the victim's photograph and uploading it to his Instagram Story with threatening captions.
Prosecuting Officer ASP Jeffery Kadison prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11 foreigners held over NYPD impersonation scam in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested 11 foreigners suspected of running an international online scam by posing as New York police officers in Bukit Ceylon on Tuesday.
The raid was conducted by Dang Wangi police at 5pm on Tuesday.
It followed information and intelligence gathered on a scam targeting victims in the United States.
Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those arrested were aged between 22 and 51 and comprised four South Africans, three Taiwanese, and one each from Mexico, Zimbabwe, Kenya and India.
"In the same operation, the raiding team seized three sets of New York Police Department (NYPD) uniforms, a New York police logo signboard and a map of New York City, which were used to deceive victims contacted through video calls.
"Also seized were 31 mobile phones, seven laptops, a monitor, a computer CPU and a router," he told a press conference today.
Azwan said digital forensic examinations and social media analysis of the seized devices indicated that the syndicate was suspected of carrying out scams by impersonating NYPD officers.
Investigations found that the suspects used artificial intelligence (AI) technology, including face-swapping techniques, background images and documents resembling official NYPD records, to convince victims that they were genuine police officers.
He said the syndicate used internet access to carry out online scams and was believed to have been operating since the middle of this year.
"The syndicate's modus operandi was to deceive victims by claiming they were involved in criminal activities and money laundering.
"All those arrested have been remanded for four days, from Nov 25 to 28," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat passes 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 by a majority voice vote.
Deputy Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Ramli Mohd Nor announced its passage after the Bill was tabled for its third reading by Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
The Bill was tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9.
Themed "Reaching for the Sky, Rooted on the Ground", the 2027 Budget outlines eight key pillars, focusing on improving people's lives and strengthening the country's resilience and future.
The fifth budget under the Madani government involves a government allocation of RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments, and RM14.2 billion in investments by federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated companies.
This brings the total allocation and investments under the 2027 Budget to RM510 billion, maintaining an expansionary fiscal policy.
The Dewan Rakyat will resume its sitting on Monday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital to reorganise parking, introduce valet service
Article:
KUANTAN: The Health Ministry has appointed a private company to reorganise parking at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital (HTAA), provide valet services and introduce parking fees as early as March.
Pahang Public Works, Transport and Health Committee chairman Datuk Razali Kassim said the company was appointed effective Nov 1 to reorganise existing parking facilities and increase capacity for hospital staff and visitors.
He said upgrading works on existing parking facilities within the hospital compound would be carried out during the first three months.
Parking fees were expected to be introduced as early as March next year, based on rates approved by the ministry, he said during his winding-up speech at the Pahang State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
The company would also be responsible for building and managing a multi-storey mechanical parking facility, with construction scheduled to begin in April next year and finish by July.
The valet service would help patients' family members find parking spaces more quickly and conveniently.
HTAA, Pahang's largest healthcare facility, currently has only 160 public parking bays, which are insufficient to meet demand.
The proposed
mechanical parking facility
is expected to provide an additional 600 bays.
Meanwhile, Razali said construction of the new women's and
children's block
in Tanjung Lumpur was 25 per cent complete as of October and scheduled for completion in December 2028.
The 376-bed block is being built at a cost of RM605 million.

Title: Power restored in parts of Tawau, Semporna and Telupid
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Electricity supply was restored to several areas in Tawau, Semporna and Telupid this afternoon following an outage caused by a disruption to the transmission line from the West Coast.
Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd said the areas in Tawau where supply had been restored included the Health Ministry clinic office and quarters, Taman Ambar Park, Taman Kuhara Jaya, Taman Hilltop along Jalan Kuhara and Hilltop Supermarket.
Other areas included the United Armed Forces Camp and 516 Territorial Army Camp, Taman Ria 1 to 9, Uni Park Industrial, Taman Jen Loong and Taman Bunga Tulip.
Supply was also restored to SMK Tawau, SMK Holy Trinity and SK Holy Trinity, as well as Gaya Commercial Centre, SUDC Commercial Centre along Jalan Kuhara and Promenade Hotel.
In Semporna, the main areas where supply had been restored included Semporna Hospital and its quarters, Bandar Seri Melur and the water village areas, as well as coastal areas including Kampung Bangau-Bangau, Kampung Panji and Kampung Air.
In Telupid, supply had been restored at Maxis Batu 4, Kampung Gaab and Kampung Gansad 01.
"Sabah Electricity greatly appreciates your patience and sincerely regrets any inconvenience caused," it said, apologising for the disruption and expressing appreciation for customers' patience and cooperation.
Meanwhile, authorities and telecommunications service providers have implemented mitigation measures to maintain connectivity along Sabah's east coast following the power disruption.
These include activating backup Starlink connections at 18 critical sites and deploying mobile and shared generator sets at 20 locations.
Sabah Electricity also shared a list of hotspot connection locations to support telecommunications service continuity, while telecommunications service providers have identified collector sites along the east coast to be prioritised for restoration.
Relevant teams have begun deploying generator sets in stages to priority sites, including critical locations and collector sites.
Sabah Electricity also implemented scheduled rotational power rationing along Sabah's east coast today due to limited local generation capacity following the T313 transmission tower incident.
The exercise aims to ensure more consumers receive electricity, maintain system stability and prevent wider supply disruptions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman survives fall from 21st floor of Pantai Ria PPR
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A woman survived a fall from the 21st floor of Block 100 at the Pantai Ria People's Housing Project (PPR) here at noon today.
Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the 29-year-old woman sustained injuries to her left leg and right hand.
"The victim was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital and is receiving treatment in the emergency ward. She suffered fractures to her left leg and right hand but is currently in stable condition," he said in a brief statement today.
[[nid:1586541]]
Hoo said preliminary investigations found that the woman was believed to have come from the Segambut area and was not a resident of the housing project.
He said her personal belongings were found on the building's 21st floor, adding that police were trying to locate her next of kin to assist with investigations.
The cause of the incident remains under investigation.
Earlier, a video went viral showing a woman dressed in a blue top and black trousers lying on the pavement, surrounded by members of the public.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan Exco to be sworn in tomorrow
Article:
SEREMBAN: The swearing-in ceremony for the new Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members is scheduled to take place at Istana Besar Seri Menanti, Kuala Pilah, tomorrow.
According to a media invitation issued by the palace, the ceremony will be held at 9am.
Earlier today, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap to discuss the current political situation in the state.
The meeting, which lasted about an hour, was also attended by Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was also granted an audience with the Ruler.

Title: DRB-HICOM swings back to RM102mil net profit in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DRB-HICOM Bhd returned to a net profit of RM101.87 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), compared with a net loss of RM15.2 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
The group's quarterly revenue rose 35.4 per cent to RM6.08 billion from RM4.49 billion previously.
For the nine months of FY26, DRB-HICOM's net profit increased to RM177.43 million from RM60.62 million a year earlier.
Revenue for the nine-month period grew 28.3 per cent to RM16.34 billion from RM12.74 billion.
The group's mobility segment recorded revenue of RM12.8 billion for the nine-month period, up 36.4 per cent.
This was supported by higher sales from Proton and the consolidation of CTRM AeroSystems following its acquisition in December 2025.
Proton sold 153,316 vehicles during the period, surpassing its full-year 2025 sales of 151,564 units, with its market share rising to 25.4 per cent from 19 per cent.
Meanwhile, the group's revenue from the banking and postal segments increased 9.5 per cent to RM1.81 billion and 8.5 per cent to RM1.46 billion respectively.
DRB-HICOM said it remains cautious about its outlook for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, amid uncertainties arising from developments in the Middle East.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petron Malaysia swings to RM109mil loss in Q3
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petron Malaysia Refining and Marketing Bhd swung into the red in the third quarter (Q3) ended Sept 30, 2026, with a net loss of RM109.02 million from a net profit of RM80.35 million a year ago.
Petron's revenue in the quarter under review rose 25 per cent to RM4.26 billion from RM3.41 billion in the corresponding quarter last year.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said its retail business in Q3 registered 4.6 million barrels, delivering two per cent sales volume growth through sales and network expansion initiatives compared to the same period last year.
However, total sales volume dropped 10 per cent to 8.4 million barrels due to lower refining production.
The benchmark Dated Brent crude oil price averaged US$97 per barrel during Q3 surging 40 per cent compared to the same period last year.
The prices dropped 23 per cent from an average price of US$108 per barrel in May to US$83 per barrel in July then climbed sharply by 41 per cent to US$117 per barrel in September driven by the expanded Middle East conflict.
"Amid a highly volatile oil price environment, the gross loss is mainly attributed to the impact of the unavailable refinery product jetty limiting production and refining margin, as well as elevated crude premium and other supply costs," it said.
For the nine-month period, the company posted a net loss of RM178.53 million from a net profit of RM201.88 million last year, while revenue rose to RM11.92 billion from RM10.34 billion.
The company noted that the global oil and gas industry continues to operate in a highly volatile environment amid ongoing geopolitical developments in the Middle East.
"Locally, the economic conditions in Malaysia remain supportive, underpinned by resilient domestic demand, investment activities and export performance.
"The company continues its commitment to support the nation's energy security by ensuring a reliable fuel supply for the domestic market. It also continues to focus on operational reliability, supply resilience and the full recovery of its refinery operations," it added.
Additionally, it said that its new product jetty at Port Dickson is on track for completion with the main platform completed in October.
The pipeline installation is in progress and expected to be completed by the end of November.

Title: Pahang MB steps in to resolve Tamil school land issue, negotiate with owner
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang government will negotiate with Pasdec Corporation Sdn Bhd to allow SJKT Ladang Jeram to remain at its current site until its new school building is completed.
Pahang Agriculture, Agro-based Industry, Biotechnology and Education Committee chairman Datuk Seri Ir Mohd Soffi Abd Razak said the state government would seek the company's cooperation to give the school sufficient time to complete its new premises before vacating the existing site.
He said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail personally intervened to ensure the school could remain until the new building was ready.
"Education is an important matter that deserves due consideration. The menteri besar has personally intervened with the landowner to allow SJKT Ladang Jeram to vacate only after its new building is completed.
"The new building, comprising an academic block and a canteen, will be constructed on a site next to SMK Sultanah Hajjah Kalsom in Bandar Damansara. The design work is being finalised," he said during his winding-up speech at the Pahang state assembly sitting.
The New Straits Times reported on Nov 21 that pupils of SJKT Ladang Jeram
faced an uncertain future
after the landowner in a letter dated Nov 13 gave the school three months to vacate the premises.
Meanwhile, Soffi said the school, which has 36 pupils and 13 teachers, would be rebuilt at a cost of RM24 million.
Pasdec issued a notice in 2022 asking the school to vacate the site but subsequently allowed it to continue operating until the new building was completed. However, construction has yet to begin.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced during the
tabling of the 2026 Budget
on Oct 10 last year that SJKT Ladang Jeram would be rebuilt.
The Pahang state assembly sitting will resume tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cops probing Pua over Najib minutes, Khoo over Friday business closure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating DAP leaders Tony Pua and Khoo Poay Tiong over separate Facebook posts following 57 reports lodged against them.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said 55 reports concerned a post by former Damansara member of parliament Pua on the declassification of Pardons Board documents relating to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The remaining two reports concerned Kota Melaka MP Khoo's post questioning a Kuala Terengganu City Council directive requiring certain businesses to close during Friday prayers.
"Both cases are still under investigation and police urge the public to refrain from speculation that could interfere with the investigations," he said in a statement.
Pua is being investigated under Section 203A of the Penal Code for disclosure of information, while Khoo's case is being investigated under Sections 298 and 505(b) of the same code, relating to deliberately wounding religious feelings and making statements likely to cause public fear or alarm.
Both are also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act for improper use of network facilities or services.
On Tuesday, Khalid said police had
yet to receive reports
on either matter and had not ruled out calling Pua over the alleged leak of minutes from a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning Najib.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had told the Dewan Rakyat that the Attorney-General's Chambers had declassified parts of the minutes to prepare its response in court proceedings concerning Najib's pardon.
Anwar denied that the government
had released the minutes to the public and called for police to investigate how the document came to be circulated.
Khoo, who is Melaka DAP chairman, had questioned the council's directive requiring certain businesses to close from 12.30pm to 2.30pm on Fridays to allow Muslims to attend prayers.
He later apologised,
acknowledging that his choice of words and tone had caused misunderstanding and offence, particularly among Muslims.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor cable theft death sparks outrage, calls for tougher penalties
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: A man who died after trying to stop cable thieves in Johor has sparked public outrage, with calls for tougher penalties against those responsible for the increasingly disruptive crime.
S. Thanus, 22, was run over on Tuesday while trying to stop suspected
cable thieves
in Taman Nusa Bestari and succumbed to his injuries on Thursday.
Johor MIC chairman K. Raven Kumar expressed condolences to Thanus's family and called on the public to alert police rather than put their lives at risk by confronting suspected
cable thieves
.
The authorities must track down those responsible, he said.
Malaysian Public Transport Users Association president Ajit Singh Johl said cable theft should be treated as a threat to national interests rather than merely an ordinary theft offence.
He said the crime was not just about the monetary value of stolen cables but also the disruption to essential services and hardship caused to commuters.
A significant proportion of cable theft cases involved railway infrastructure, including MRT and LRT lines, where damaged cables could disrupt public transport operations, he said.
"Cable theft should not be treated as ordinary theft. It should be treated as treason because the damage goes far beyond the value of the cables stolen.
"The crime is not just against the utility provider but against millions of consumers and public transport users who suffer when services are disrupted," he said.
Ajit Singh said penalties for cable theft needed to be reviewed through legislative amendments, warning that the crime would continue if punishments did not reflect the extent of the damage caused.
"Until the punishment for cable theft is reviewed, this will keep happening. We need to take it much more seriously than standard theft because of the wider consequences," he said.
Cable theft along rail tracks has been on the rise, with
Prasarana Malaysia Bhd
recording 72 cases last year, up 68 per cent from 42 in 2024. The thefts caused RM20.6 million in losses over three years and disrupted rail services.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Non-Sarawakian DAP federal leaders to sit out state polls campaign
Article:
KUCHING: Non-Sarawakian DAP ministers and deputy ministers will not campaign in the 13th Sarawak state election, with the state chapter taking charge of its own campaign, said Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen.
He said the decision was made in the spirit of the Madani government and out of respect for the party's coalition partners at federal level.
"Sarawak DAP will lead the campaign on the ground, with our own leaders, our own members and our own message. Our record and our commitment to the people of Sarawak will speak for themselves," he said in a statement.
Chong said the decision was part of a consensus reached following his meeting with DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke in Kuala Lumpur today, after Parti Keadilan Rakyat's (PKR) withdrawal from the state election.
In the spirit of democracy, he said Sarawak DAP maintained its position to contest in the upcoming state election.
"This isn't a new concession. It is a principle Sarawak DAP has always upheld. Matters concerning Sarawak are decided by Sarawak DAP solely.
"That has always included the number of seats we contest, the choice of candidates, and the signing of the watikah to contest under the DAP logo. These decisions are made here in Sarawak, by Sarawak DAP," he said.
Chong said the DAP Central Executive Committee had also reaffirmed its full respect for Sarawak DAP's autonomy and would abide by the arrangement.
DAP has so far confirmed that it will contest 12 seats in the state election.
Meanwhile, Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) has named candidates for all 82 seats, Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS) 26, Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK) 12 and Parti Aspirasi Rakyat Sarawak (Aspirasi) one, while Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) has announced its intention to contest three seats.
The Election Commission has fixed Nov 28 for nomination day, followed by early voting on Dec 8 and polling on Dec 12.

Title: Brief downpour leaves Kampung Makam under water
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Kampung Makam was hit by flash floods following a heavy afternoon downpour today, with nearby Kampung Dodol also reportedly affected.
The rain, which began in the late afternoon, caused water levels to rise rapidly, inundating low-lying areas.
A resident took to TikTok Live to share footage of the situation in Kampung Makam, showing floodwaters reaching an adult's calf level at the compound.
He said about 20 houses were located in the village and told viewers he was moving his car to higher ground.
"It did not rain for long but our surroundings have been flooded. This is possibly worsened by the high tide phenomenon," he said.
In the comments section, a resident of nearby Kampung Dodol also reported similar flooding.
Rain was also reported in several parts of the mainland.
No evacuations had been reported so far, while local authorities and emergency personnel were monitoring the situation.
Penang residents have been advised to remain alert for thunderstorms and king tides expected to affect the state until tomorrow.
State Fire and Rescue Department director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said residents should remain vigilant during the ongoing
northeast monsoon
, particularly those living in low-lying and coastal areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muslims must speak out against corruption, misconduct, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Muslims in Malaysia must set an example by embracing knowledge, upholding justice and having the courage to speak out against corruption and misconduct, even when the perpetrators hide behind the name of religion.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said young people must also have the courage to ask questions and examine the basis of every argument before accepting it.
"During the Dialog Negara, I was asked about religious controversies that divide society and how the people could distinguish between religious enlightenment and political views presented as though they were religious rulings.
"I stressed that knowledge is the foremost prerequisite for Islamic preaching. I knew Sheikh Yusuf al-Qaradawi as a teacher of profound knowledge, and I never heard him pass judgement on others arbitrarily," he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar said such an attitude should be emulated, particularly when some quarters readily issued fatwas without scriptural evidence to legitimise their political agendas, even in support of detrimental practices.
Last night, Anwar addressed various questions concerning government policies, considerations and decisions on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight, which was also simulcast on RTMKlik, Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IOI Properties' Q1 earnings ease, but hospitality profit soars sixfold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Properties Group Bhd's net profit fell 8.2 per cent to RM609.54 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27) from RM664.33 million a year earlier.
Revenue rose 16 per cent to RM1.13 billion from RM968.7 million, driven by stronger contributions from its property investment and hospitality and leisure segments.
Excluding exceptional items, IOI Properties' underlying earnings improved by 25 per cent, supported by contributions from South Beach office tower and JW Marriott in Singapore, as well as improved occupancy at IOI Central Boulevard Towers.
Hospitality and leisure was among the strongest performers, with operating profit increasing more than sixfold.
This wss supported by higher hotel occupancy and average room rates in Malaysia and Singapore.
In Malaysia, W Kuala Lumpur and Le Meridien Putrajaya recorded occupancy rates of 87 per cent each, while Moxy Putrajaya achieved 82 per cent.
Group chief executive officer Datuk Lee Yeow Seng said the performance reflected the group's strategy to diversify its income streams and strengthen recurring earnings across its three core business segments.
The property development segment recorded sales of RM454.2 million during the quarter, with Malaysia contributing RM388.3 million, or 86 per cent, of the total.
The group's unbilled sales stood at RM2.46 billion, providing earnings visibility over the near to medium term.
The proposed sale of industrial land at IOI Industrial Park Banting to Bridge Data Centres is on track for completion by the fourth quarter of calendar year 2026.
Meanwhile, the property investment segment benefited from resilient rental demand at its retail malls and offices, including IOI City Mall and IOI Mall Puchong.
The group's acquisition of Asia Square Tower 2 in Singapore, completed on Sept 17, adds 2.58 million sq ft of net lettable office space to its portfolio.
Separately, the listing of IOIPG Reit on Nov 25 raised about RM2 billion, strengthening the group's balance sheet and supporting its capital recycling initiatives.
Lee said the group remained positive about its outlook for the rest of FY27, underpinned by its diversified property portfolio, healthy unbilled sales and growing recurring income.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lagenda Properties's Q3 earnings rise 38.8pct to RM62mil on RM404.5mil revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lagenda Properties Bhd's net profit rose 38.8 per cent to RM62 million in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), from RM44.7 million a year earlier, on the back of higher revenue.
Revenue surged 58.7 per cent to RM404.5 million from RM254.9 million, while pre-tax profit increased 54.5 per cent to RM95.3 million from RM61.7 million.
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue increased 32.3 per cent to RM1 billion from RM758.2 million, while net profit grew 21 per cent to RM162.7 million from RM134.5 million.
The property development segment remained the group's largest revenue contributor, recording RM359.9 million in revenue for the third quarter, up 56.7 per cent from a year earlier.
Lagenda also recorded its highest-ever quarterly confirmed sales of RM573.5 million, bringing confirmed sales for the nine-month period to RM1.45 billion.
As of September this year, its unbilled sales stood at a record RM1.93 billion, while bookings amounted to RM480.7 million, providing visibility for future revenue.
The company had an unlaunched landbank of 1,559.5 hectares, with an estimated remaining gross development value of RM9.5 billion.
Lagenda said it would focus on construction progress and upcoming launches across its existing townships in Johor, Kedah, Negri Sembilan and Pahang, while maintaining a disciplined approach to landbanking, project execution and cost management.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's gender gap narrows slightly on economic gains – DOSM
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's gender gap narrowed slightly in 2025, with the Malaysia Gender Gap Index (MGGI) rising to 0.711 from 0.708 the previous year, driven mainly by improvements in women's economic participation and opportunities.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said the economic participation and opportunity subindex increased to 0.728 from 0.703 in 2024.
Women's labour force participation rate edged up to 56.6 per cent from 56.5 per cent, while their mean monthly salaries and wages rose to RM3,635 from RM3,499.
The number of women working as legislators, senior officials and managers also increased to 241,000 from 219,000, while those in professional and technical occupations rose to 1.8 million from 1.7 million.
"The MGGI measures the gender gap between women and men in four areas, namely economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment," DOSM said in its MGGI 2026 report released today.
A score of 1.000 indicates full equality between women and men.
DOSM said the educational attainment subindex stood at 1.064 in 2025, compared with 1.073 in 2024.
"Female students recorded higher gross enrolment rates at the secondary and tertiary levels, at 95.9 per cent and 57.1 per cent respectively, while the rate for both males and females at the primary level was 99.7 per cent," it said.
The health and survival subindex stood at 0.957 in 2025, with women's life expectancy at birth rising to 77.8 years from 65.6 years in 1970.
However, political empowerment remained the weakest area, with a score of just 0.094.
DOSM said women accounted for only 15.6 per cent of ministerial positions and 13.5 per cent of seats in the Dewan Rakyat.
"This reflects the continuing challenges in achieving gender balance in political leadership and decision-making in Malaysia," it said.
At the state level, Kuala Lumpur recorded the highest MGGI score at 0.781, followed by Labuan at 0.756 and Putrajaya at 0.754.
Five states recorded scores below the national level of 0.711, namely Melaka (0.707), Terengganu (0.706), Pahang (0.704), Sarawak (0.698) and Johor (0.693).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SD Property's profit dips in Q3, but nine-month performance still strong
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd's net profit fell 29.3 per cent to RM118.9 million in the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26) from RM168.2 million a year earlier.
Revenue declined 11.8 per cent to RM1.07 billion from RM1.21 billion, while profit before tax (PBT) dropped 26.1 per cent to RM192.6 million from RM260.7 million.
However, the property developer's nine-month performance remained strong, with net profit rising 39.4 per cent year-on-year to RM599.7 million from RM430.2 million.
SD Property's pre-tax profit for the nine-month period increased 25.7 per cent to RM828.2 million from RM659.1 million, despite revenue easing 3.7 per cent to RM3.03 billion from RM3.15 billion.
The group attributed its stronger nine-month profitability to higher contributions from its investment and asset management (IAM) portfolio, which recorded a 63.8 per cent increase in revenue to RM221.6 million and more than doubled its pre-tax profit to RM213.6 million, supported by recurring income from data centre and retail assets.
The property development segment remained its largest contributor, recording revenue of RM2.7 billion and pre-tax profit of RM615.9 million.
Group managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Azmir Merican said the record nine-month profitability reflected the growing contribution of recurring income assets alongside the group's township and industrial developments.
For the nine months, the group recorded RM3.7 billion in property launches and RM2.5 billion in sales. Unbilled sales stood at RM3.6 billion as at Sept 30, 2026.
The group also launched its maiden Melbourne development, Aurum, with an estimated gross development value of A$1.08 billion (RM3.2 billion), and secured shareholders' approval for a proposed land acquisition in Kulai, Johor, for a township with an estimated GDV of RM3 billion.
The group is also preparing for a potential industrial and logistics real estate investment trust (Reit) listing as it expands its assets under management, although it ruled out a listing in 2027.
President and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Azmir Merican said the group was working towards the Reit but had yet to determine its listing timeline or disclose the assets to be included.
He said the group would consider recycling its capital through a Reit once its asset portfolio had grown sufficiently and generated attractive yields, adding that it was still at an early stage of preparations.
"We do feel that as we build our assets under management and get to a point where the yields are attractive, it will be an appropriate time to recycle capital," he said.
He added that it was too early to speculate on whether the listing would take place in 2028.
For FY26, SD Property is targeting full-year launches of about RM5 billion and aims to grow its assets under management to more than RM10 billion by 2028.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From remote Batang Rajang to luxury tables: Sarawak’s prized empurau commands up to RM2,500 per kg
Article:
SIBU, Nov 26 — The landing of an empurau weighing over 12 kilogrammes at the premises of Sarawak wild fish supplier Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong here proves that the species is not merely an ordinary river catch, but a luxury commodity worth tens of thousands of ringgit.
Known scientifically as Tor tambroides, the fish, which fetches RM2,000 to RM2,500 per kilogramme in the international market, continues to cement its dominance in the exclusive culinary segment.
The iconic species is now sought after by high-end restaurants, wholesalers, and the elite in Hong Kong, China, and Singapore, as well as the Peninsular Malaysia market including Kuala Lumpur, Perak, and Penang.
Behind that extraordinary price tag, the journey of the “King of the River” begins far in the remote upstream areas before passing through a chain of fishermen, suppliers, and air logistics to reach the dining tables of high-income earners.
For Jeferry, 41, the business is not merely about chasing profits through trading exotic fish, but also ensuring that every bit of hard work by local fishermen receives a fair and lucrative return.
“This empurau has its own uniqueness with fine, tender, and sweet-textured flesh as well as a fatty belly, while its special aroma comes from its natural diet as it feeds only on wild forest fruits such as engkabang and ensurai.
“A large-sized fish can fetch tens of thousands of ringgit, even enough to buy an used car, depending on its weight and the market,” he told Bernama recently.
He said the uniqueness of the empurau, which inhabits fast-flowing upstream rivers, also lies in its growth period, which takes more than 10 years.
Fresh supplies are obtained directly from fishermen’s bases in the interior such as Ulu Kapit and Baleh, with the nearly 600-kilometre Batang Rajang river basin remaining the main habitat for various high-value freshwater species.
Close cooperation with local fishermen, including Leanard Anak Lenggie and Gamas Iban from Kapit, forms the backbone of his operational stability, which demands swift action as soon as the catch is brought ashore.
He said in the wild fish trade, there is no room for any delay as timeliness is the absolute determining factor in maintaining the freshness and highest-grade quality of the empurau.
He noted that demand for the premium species usually surges ahead of festive seasons such as Christmas and Chinese New Year to be served as a special dish for families and celebratory gatherings.
Apart from empurau, Jeferry’s business premises located at Jalan Long Bridge also supply various other freshwater species including patin buah, tapah, jelawat, semah, tengadak, terubuk, sebarau, giant freshwater prawns (udang galah), ketutu, and baung.
This variety allows his business to cater to the tastes and budgets of customers from various backgrounds, rather than relying on empurau alone.
Commenting on export matters, Jeferry said shipments outside Sarawak via air freight to maintain freshness also affect the selling price, in addition to requiring permits, veterinary documents, and shipping declarations.
His experience in managing shipping as well as import-export businesses has also been an advantage in handling documentation and logistics coordination to meet customer needs.
Ahead of the 13th Sarawak State Election, the Sibu native, who will cast his ballot in the Bukit Assek state constituency, hopes the potential of the river fisheries sector, particularly high-value species like empurau, will be given due attention by elected representatives as one of the state’s economic drivers.
He said continuous support in terms of infrastructure, basic amenities, and market access is crucial to ensure Sarawak’s river produce continues to bring greater benefits to fishing communities and the rural economy.
“I believe efforts to strengthen market access, transport facilities, as well as networks between operators and suppliers also have the potential to help this sector grow, thereby ensuring Sarawak’s river produce continues to secure a place in both domestic and international premium markets,” he said.
Bukit Assek is one of two state constituencies in the Lanang parliamentary constituency, alongside Dudong, involved in the Sarawak State Election.
The Election Commission (EC) has set this Saturday (November 28) as nomination day, followed by early voting on December 8 and polling day on December 12.
